taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid local time.

**Checking the date:** The page says "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026" and "six days from today, on Friday." Six days from Saturday Oct 24 would be Friday, Oct 30, 2026. That's consistent (Oct 30, 2026 is indeed a Friday).

**The deadline:** Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

**Time zone conversion:**
- PT (Pacific Time) on Oct 30, 2026 is PDT (daylight saving still in effect; US DST ends Nov 1, 2026). PDT = UTC−7.
- 11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 − (−7) → 23:59 + 7 = 06:59 UTC on Oct 31, 2026.
- Madrid (Spain) on Oct 31, 2026: European DST ends Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.
- 06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 on Oct 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Deadline: Monday, November 2, 2026, 10:00 AM Los Angeles time.

Los Angeles in early November: DST ends November 1, 2026, so by Nov 2 LA is on PST (UTC−8).

10:00 AM PST = 18:00 UTC.

Madrid in early November is on CET (UTC+1), since European DST ends October 25, 2026.

18:00 UTC + 1 = 19:00 Madrid time, Monday November 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time.

Adding 48 hours lands on Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00.

Note: Daylight saving time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. At 03:00 CEST, clocks fall back to 02:00 CET. So the 48-hour span crosses the DST change, but since we're measuring a fixed duration of 48 hours and expressing the end in local wall-clock time, the fall-back adds an extra hour of elapsed clock-time offset.

Let me compute carefully using UTC:
- Start: Oct 24, 18:00 CEST = 16:00 UTC
- Add 48 hours = Oct 26, 16:00 UTC
- On Oct 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), so local time = 17:00.

Since you're in Madrid, this is your local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid local time.

**Start time:** October 26, 2026, 10:00 AM PT

**Deadline:** 72 hours later = 3 days later = October 29, 2026, 10:00 AM PT

**Convert PT to Madrid time:**

First, check the time zones on October 29, 2026:
- **US Pacific Time:** Daylight saving ends on the first Sunday of November 2026 (November 1, 2026). So on October 29, PT is still on PDT (UTC−7).
- **Madrid (Central European Time):** DST ends on the last Sunday of October 2026 (October 25, 2026). So by October 29, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**Calculate offset:**
- October 29, 2026, 10:00 AM PDT = UTC−7 → 17:00 UTC
- Madrid CET (UTC+1) → 17:00 + 1 = 18:00

**Deadline in Madrid:** October 29, 2026, 18:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close: October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (EDT, UTC-4, since DST ends November 1, 2026).

Results: 36 hours later.

Let me work in UTC first.
- Close: Oct 31, 2026, 23:59 EDT = Nov 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC
- Add 36 hours: Nov 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC

Madrid: In late October/November, Spain switches off DST on October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
- Nov 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = Nov 2, 2026, 16:59

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Unix timestamp 1791788340 seconds.

Converting to UTC:
1791788340 / 86400 ≈ 20738.29 days since epoch.

Let me compute precisely. 
- 1791788340 seconds = days: 1791788340 ÷ 86400 = 20738 days remainder.
- 20738 × 86400 = 1791763200.
- Remainder: 1791788340 − 1791763200 = 25140 seconds.
- 25140 s = 6 h (21600) + 3540 s = 6:59:00.

Day 20738 from 1970-01-01 (day 0).
20738 days ≈ 56.79 years. Let me find the date.

From 1970 to 2026 is 56 years. Days from 1970-01-01 to 2026-01-01:
- 56 years with leap years (1972...2024) = 14 leap years.
- 56 × 365 + 14 = 20440 + 14 = 20454 days.

Remaining: 20738 − 20454 = 284 days into 2026.
2026 is not a leap year.
- Jan 31, Feb 28 (59), Mar 31 (90), Apr 30 (120), May 31 (151), Jun 30 (181), Jul 31 (212), Aug 31 (243), Sep 30 (273), Oct (284).
- Day 273 = Sep 30, so day 284 = Oct 11.

So UTC: 2026-10-11 06:59:00.

Tokyo is UTC+9: add 9 hours → 15:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid time zone: In late October 2026, I need to determine if daylight saving time is still active.

EU daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. The clocks go back at 03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET on that Sunday.

The deadline is 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z (UTC).

- CEST = UTC+2, CET = UTC+1
- The DST change happens at 01:00 UTC (which is 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET).
- At 02:30 UTC, the change has already occurred, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this.

**Find the last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026 has 31 days. October 31, 2026 is a Saturday, so the last Sunday is October 25, 2026.

**Deadline in Pacific Time:**
11:59 PM PT on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

**Determine Pacific offset on that date:**
US Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). So on October 25, 2026, Pacific Time is still on PDT (UTC−7).

So deadline = 23:59 PDT = 23:59 + 7 = 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026.

**Convert to Madrid time:**
Europe changes clocks on the last Sunday of October — October 25, 2026 — when CEST (UTC+2) ends and CET (UTC+1) begins at 03:00 local time. By October 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

So 06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 on October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this.

**When US DST ends in 2026:** Daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's **November 1, 2026**.

**Eastern Time at that moment:** At 2:00 AM local on that day, clocks fall back from EDT (UTC-4) to EST (UTC-5). The deadline is 12:00 noon, which is after the change, so it's in **EST = UTC-5**.

- 12:00 noon EST = 17:00 UTC

**Lima, Peru time:** Peru uses PET = UTC-5 year-round (no DST).

- 17:00 UTC − 5 = 12:00 (noon) local time, on November 1, 2026.

Since EST and PET are both UTC-5, the local time matches: 12:00 noon.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12. The deadline is the end of December 31, 2026, in the last timezone.

"December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" = January 1, 2027, 00:00 at UTC-12, which equals January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.

Tokyo is UTC+9, so add 9 hours: January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in New York time (since you're traveling there and need NY time).

**Step 1: Sydney time on the deadline**
5:00 PM (17:00) Sydney time, October 5, 2026.

**Step 2: Determine Sydney's UTC offset on that date**
Australian Eastern Time. Sydney observes Daylight Saving Time starting the first Sunday of October 2026, which is October 4, 2026. So by October 5, Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11).

17:00 AEDT = 17:00 − 11:00 = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

**Step 3: Convert to New York time**
New York is on Eastern Daylight Time in early October 2026 (DST ends November 1, 2026). EDT = UTC−4.

06:00 UTC − 4:00 = 02:00 EDT on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
